## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(paletteer)
library(cowplot)
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}

```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
cc_names <- c(
"Unknown",
"Digalactosyldiacylglycerol",
"Linear polyketides",
"Sesquiterpenoids",
"Carotenoids (C40)",
"Oligopeptides",      
"Diacylglyceryl-carboxyhydroxymethylcholines",    
"Sphingolipids",      
"Triacylglycerols",       
"Polyprenols" ,        
"Monogalactosyldiacylglycerol",
"Diacylglycerols",
"Glycerophospholipids",
"Fatty amides",
"Meroterpenoids",
"Glycerolipids",
"Steroids"
)

stepped_seq_5 <- c(
  "darkgrey",
  "#990F0F", "#CC5252", "#E67E7E", "#FFB2B2", # Reds (1:5)
  "#99700F", "#CCA852", "#E6C77E", "#FFE8B2", # Yellows/Browns (6:10)
  "#1F990F", "#60CC52", "#8AE67E", "#BCFFB2", # Greens (11:15)
  "#710F99", "#A852CC", "#C77EE6", "#E9B2FF", # Purples (16:20)
  "#990F20", "#CC5260", "#E67E8A", "#FFB2BC"  # Crimsons/Roses (21:25)
)


c25 <- c(
  "gray70","dodgerblue2", "#E31A1C", "green4", "#6A3D9A", "#FF7F00",
  "black", "gold1", "skyblue2", "#FB9A99", "palegreen2",
  "#CAB2D6", "#FDBF6F",  "khaki2", "maroon",
  "orchid1", "deeppink1", "blue1", "steelblue4", "darkturquoise",
  "green1", "yellow4", "yellow3", "darkorange4", "brown"
)

# 2. Extract the exact number of colors needed from a paletteer palette
# Format syntax: "package::palette"
my_colors <- paletteer_d("dichromat::SteppedSequential_5", n = length(cc_names))

# 3. Pair the names with the colors using setNames()
named_palette <- setNames(as.character(c25), cc_names)


```

```{r}
print(named_palette)
```

Dummy legend for variable importance plots

```{r, fig.width = 15}

feats_in_vip <- feats_stats_oculina |>
  filter(compound_superclass %in% cc_names)

feat_stat_plot <- ggplot(feats_in_vip, aes(x = sum, y = compound_superclass, fill = compound_superclass)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = named_palette) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

feat_stat_plot

vip_leg <- get_legend(feat_stat_plot)

vip_leg
```

dummy legend for figure 3

```{r}
pcoa_dum <-ggplot(data = pcoa_df_ocu_fin_depthsa_no_out, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = depth_sa)) + 
  geom_point() +
 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Shallow Aposymbiotic" = "orange", "Shallow Symbiotic" = "blue", "Deep Aposymbiotic" = "hotpink3")) +
  
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.margin=ggplot2::margin(t=5,b=2,r=5,l=5,unit="pt"),
        ) +
  #theme(legend.position = "none") +

  labs(
       x = paste("PC1 ", sprintf("%.1f%%", variance_explained_fin_depthsa_no_out[1])),
       y = paste("PC2 ", sprintf("%.1f%%", variance_explained_fin_depthsa_no_out[2])),
       color = "Symbiotic State"
       ) +
  theme(plot.margin=ggplot2::margin(t=8,b=8,r=15,l=20,unit="pt")) +
  theme(legend.position =  "bottom") 



   
pcoa_oculina_fin_depthsa_no_out
pcoa_legend <- get_legend(pcoa_dum)
pcoa_legend
```

Figure (2): Ella's two physio box plots, my richness box plot, my PCoA no outliers

```{r}
#chla_nov_depth_sa_box
#sym_nov_depth_sa_box
#richness_3_cat_box
#pcoa_oculina_fin_depthsa_no_out


fig2 <- plot_grid(chla_nov_depth_sa_box, sym_nov_depth_sa_box, richness_3_cat_box, pcoa_oculina_fin_depthsa_no_out, pcoa_legend,
                  nrow=3, 
                  rel_widths=c(1, 1, 1, 1, 0.2), 
                  axis = "tblr", 
                  align="v", 
                  label_size = 8, 
                  labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))

fig2

ggsave(plot = fig2, "fig2_01.pdf", width=8, height=10.0, units=c("in"), dpi=300)
#print(fig3)
```
